launches.body:
**TL;DR:** [Boxes.dev](https://boxes.dev/launch-yc) is a cloud environment for coding with AI. Move Claude Code and Codex off your laptop, run unlimited copies of your dev environment in the cloud so agents can test their own work, and massively improve your productivity.

<https://youtu.be/6a3Zk0Z5iYE>

Hey everyone — we’re Nick and Drew. We met at MIT, and previously built and scaled Gem (YC S17) to over a $1B valuation together.

We’re excited to officially launch Boxes.dev: a place to work with coding agents 100% in the cloud, using your existing Claude Code and Codex subscriptions.

**The problem**

It’s increasingly normal to run 5-10 Claude Code or Codex agents at once – but localhost just wasn't built for that. Your agents stop working when you close your laptop. Picking up work from your phone is awkward. Worktrees are a pain to manage. And if you want your 10 agents to actually test their changes live in your app? Good luck fitting all that onto your laptop’s memory and CPU.

There are plenty of “cloud agent” products, but most can’t run your full dev environment or need hard-to-maintain setup scripts to do so. Without a dev setup, you get neutered agents that can’t test their work live. Would you let an engineer write code without a working dev environment?

**A cloud dev environment for AI coding**

These pain points are why we built Boxes.dev: a cloud computer for each coding agent, full development environments that can actually run your app, and all the convenience of localhost.

We feel strongly that your dev environment shouldn’t sell you tokens or dictate which harness you use. That’s why we run Claude Code and Codex unmodified, and let you bring your subscriptions and API keys with you.

**How Boxes.dev works**

1. Paste a short setup prompt into your local Claude Code or Codex, and your agent ports your dev environment to the cloud.
2. Start agents from the Boxes.dev desktop app, your phone, Slack, Linear, and more.
3. Work with your agents like normal! Each agent gets its own machine, and can test its work end to end in your app and send screenshots. Or you can open your local browser to localhost:<your-port> and manually test their work via port forwarding.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=126175&key=user_uploads/295276/762b3b41-767a-446e-876f-3848cd0f2ccd)

\
**The future is in the cloud**

Coding workflows of the future won’t fit on one engineer’s laptop. We’re helping teams assemble software factories, run agent swarms, and collaborate better in the agentic coding era. A few examples of what’s possible:

* One customer ran a swarm of over 200 agents on more than 100 machines to build a piece of complex software from scratch. Agents on Boxes.dev can message each other, spawn other agents and machines, and self-organize, so this was easy to set up.
* Many customers have built software factories, triggering work on Boxes.dev via API and automations, passing tasks across multiple steps, and outputting fully tested PRs for final review.
* We’re using Boxes.dev ourselves to continually add new features and improvements, and our agents notice when teammates' agents are doing related work and message them to coordinate conflicts or pass helpful tips.

**Engineer? Running a dev team?**

We sincerely believe that cloud is the future of all coding. If you're not a cloud convert yet, we'd love for you to try it out. 

If you’re a YC company or founder, check out our [Bookface deal](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/deals/18232); otherwise use [boxes.dev/launch-yc](https://boxes.dev/launch-yc) for 3 free months of Pro, on us.

And if you're just starting to think about remote dev environments for your team, we're always happy to talk architecture, and also share best practices from the most AI-pilled engineers. And if you know a CTO whose team writes most of their code with agents, we'd love an intro.

Feel free to reach out!
